original.target_description: Study 5 independently manipulates target race and ecology in eight between-subject conditions, measuring five life-history stereotype domains and an aggregate composite. The locator p. 3 and broad description do not distinguish the several race, ecology, within-race, or within-ecology contrasts or composite versus component outcomes.

n.sample_role: Unselected candidate: 302 participants signed up across all eight conditions; no contrast-specific analytic N established.
n.exclusions: No contrast-specific exclusions or final condition counts established in the inspected Study 5 methods/results.
n.quote: Three hundred and two (134 females; mean age, 19.58 y; SD, 1.70; 55% white, 17% Asian American, 16% Hispanic, 5% African American) participants signed up for a study on person perception as part of introductory psychology course requirements. ... Participants were thus randomly assigned to one of eight experimental conditions.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a PMC primary-research article parse (SOURCE https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4720338/), headed Ecology-driven stereotypes override race stereotypes, by Keelah E G Williams, Oliver Sng, and Steven L Neuberg, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1519401113. It contains abstract, main results, Methods, SI Text, and references, rather than only an abstract or a secondary account. Header publication 2015 Dec 28 and issue date 2016 Jan 12 explain the reference year/volume timing. Identity matches the supplied original reference; this is not the replication source. No PDF supplied. Target ambiguity: study number matches Study 5, but broad description and p. 3 fail to identify outcome/contrast. No statistic selected by row order or numeric matching. Printed composite candidates (effect and p from the same respective contrast): desperate versus hopeful ecology without race, d = 1.10, P < 0.001; black versus white without ecology, d = 0.63, P < 0.001; desperate ecology/no race versus black/no ecology, d = 0.30, P = 0.012; white desperate versus white hopeful, d = 0.95, P < 0.001; black desperate versus black hopeful, d = 0.96, P < 0.001. Composite hopeful/no race versus white/no ecology gives P = 0.12 without printed d in the associated main-text sentence. Composite white versus black within desperate ecology gives P = 0.59 and within hopeful ecology P = 0.69; no d printed with those sentences. SI Text also gives domain-specific contrasts and a grouped composite statement all P > 0.59, whereas main text gives the separate exact p values above; these were not merged. Component candidates include no-ecology black-versus-white sexual unrestrictedness d = 0.24/P = 0.036, impulsivity d = 0.40/P = 0.001, opportunism d = 0.51/P < 0.001, own education d = 0.54/P < 0.001, children d = 0.58/P < 0.001, plus within-race ecology contrasts. Metric d is preserved as printed; no conversion or assumed standardisation. N candidate only: Methods says 302 signed up and random assignment to eight conditions. That whole-study number is not an established analytic N for any one of the candidate pairwise tests. No final mutually exclusive condition counts are provided in the inspected Study 5 text, so no N sum or df inference was performed. Original status done indicates inspection completed, not that a unique target was resolved. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
